triage_context.environment: Internet-facing web service (HTTP is untrusted); callers are authenticated end users
threat_model: Tenant-to-tenant data leakage / tampering across accounts

findings.title: deleteBeneficiary deletes by id alone, ignoring caller identity (IDOR)
preconditions: Attacker must be an authenticated user (any registered account; self-serve signup)
Attacker must know or guess the target beneficiary's UUID (not exposed by id-enumeration, but can leak via logs, referrer, shared screen, support tickets, or a future endpoint)
findings.threat_match: Tenant-to-tenant data leakage / tampering across accounts
findings.rationale: All 3 independent verifiers confirm TRUE_POSITIVE at confidence 9/10. deleteBeneficiaryHandler (beneficiaries.controller.ts:26) passes req.user!.id straight through to beneficiariesService.deleteBeneficiary, reached via DELETE /:id (beneficiaries.routes.ts:9,13) gated only by requireAuth, which verifies the session but performs no per-resource ownership check. deleteBeneficiary(_callerUserId, id) (beneficiaries.service.ts:42-51) never references the underscore-prefixed _callerUserId parameter and executes prisma.beneficiary.delete({ where: { id } }) with no ownerUserId predicate. listBeneficiaries and addBeneficiary in the same file both correctly scope by ownerUserId, confirming this is an inconsistency/omission rather than intended design. Severity derived as MEDIUM rather than the scanner's claimed HIGH because exploitation requires an authenticated attacker (not unauthenticated-remote) plus knowledge of a specific target UUID -- 2 preconditions, authenticated access per the precondition/access-level table -- though the blast radius (silent cross-account data destruction) argues for prompt remediation regardless of the derived label.
findings.owner_hint: component: beneficiaries/; top committer chandra sekhar (per git log)
